entities.title: NoneOf, because None is a keyword
entities.summary: The none case of an outcome is called NoneOf.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §3 names the five outcome cases Unique, Multiple, None, Unsupported and Invalid, as frozen dataclasses in Python.
entities.decision: The none case is the frozen dataclass NoneOf; its wire status is still none.
entities.rationale: None is a Python keyword and can't name a class.

entities.title: Period.of_days and TemporalContext(rules)
entities.summary: Two names differ from the shared naming table, as docs/library-api.md §6 records.
entities.context: The shared table names Period.Days(30) and TemporalContext.With(rules).
entities.decision: Period's static constructors are of_years, of_months, of_weeks and of_days (with Period.of and Period(...)); a context is made with TemporalContext(rules) or TemporalContext.with_rules(rules).
entities.rationale: A days classmethod would clash with the days component field, and with is a keyword.

entities.title: Years are Python ints
entities.summary: A year has no size limit: it is a Python int in typed values and a decimal string in JSON.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §1 requires arbitrary-precision years and names int for Python.
entities.decision: Typed values hold years as int; calendar arithmetic goes through day numbers computed with integer arithmetic for any year.
entities.rationale: Python's int is arbitrary precision, so no separate big-integer type is needed.
entities.details: The one bound is Python's int–string conversion limit (implementations/python/.dev/limitations.json, int-string-limit).

entities.title: Constructor errors are ValueErrors
entities.summary: A constructor given a value that can't exist raises OutcomeError, a subclass of ValueError.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §1 asks constructors to raise the language's ordinary argument error, and names ValueError for Python; single() needs an error too.
entities.decision: One exception, OutcomeError(ValueError), serves both: it carries the wire status and the diagnostics.
entities.rationale: It behaves as datetime.date does for 30 February (README), and the reason stays a diagnostic code rather than a message.

entities.title: The typed layer calls the JSON layer
entities.summary: Every typed operation builds its value's JSON and calls the JSON-level function underneath.
entities.context: 0.3 adds the typed layer on top of the unchanged 0.2 JSON layer, which the shared fixtures test; docs/library-api.md §2 says libraries should call the 0.2 functions rather than re-implement them.
entities.decision: Typed values convert to JSON on each operation and read the answer back (values._typed, outcome_of); constructors run the JSON layer's checks.
entities.rationale: So the two layers can't disagree (values.py's module docstring).
entities.details: Every typed call pays for building and validating JSON; no measurements are recorded here.

entities.title: Typed overloads for month-end policies; wire strings accepted
entities.summary: add_months and add_years have two typed overloads, and every policy parameter also takes its wire string.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §2 makes AddMonths(n) partial and AddMonths(n, MonthEnd.Constrain) total, and §4 lets Python accept the literal strings through a typed parameter.
entities.decision: typing.overload declares Outcome[T] without a policy and T with Constrain (MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN or "constrain"); any other policy in that form raises ValueError. MonthEnd, Gap and Overlap are str enums, and MonthEndLike, GapLike and OverlapLike accept the enum or a Literal string.
entities.rationale: A type checker knows which call returns an outcome, and rejecting is what the call without a policy does (README).

sources.symbol: Total operations return values, partial ones return outcomes

entities.title: Order compares values; equality compares representations
entities.summary: 09:30 and 09:30:00 are unequal, yet each is <= the other.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §1: equality is representation equality, comparisons treat a missing second as 0, and ties break by representation only where a language requires order to agree with equality.
entities.decision: __eq__ is the dataclass's field equality; __lt__, __le__, __gt__ and __ge__ go through the JSON layer's compare, with no tie-break.
entities.rationale: Python doesn't require ordering to agree with equality, so no tie-break is needed.

entities.title: A naive datetime is a floating wall time
entities.summary: A datetime without tzinfo is never read as local time.
entities.context: Python's naive datetime is often used to mean "local time on this machine"; docs/everyday-api.md's interop rules forbid reading the host's zone.
entities.decision: from_datetime turns a naive datetime only into a floating wall time; asking for an instant, an offset or a zone is unsupported (local-zone). ZoneInfo("localtime"), ZoneInfo from a file and tzinfo classes other than timezone and ZoneInfo are refused, and astimezone() is never called without an argument.
entities.rationale: Reading it as an instant or offset would need the host's local zone, which UTV never consults (native.py's module docstring).

entities.title: Zoned datetimes use the caller's ZoneInfo
entities.summary: Converting a zoned value to datetime takes a ZoneInfo from the caller, and its tz data decides gaps and folds.
entities.context: A ZonedIntent names a zone id; a datetime needs a tzinfo, and only zoneinfo can supply one for an IANA zone.
entities.decision: to_datetime requires tz=ZoneInfo with the same key, picks the fold from the asserted offset, and answers none or multiple from that ZoneInfo; from_datetime asserts the offset that ZoneInfo gives. The library never constructs a ZoneInfo.
entities.rationale: The library doesn't read the host's tz database (to_datetime's docstring; "The ZoneInfo the caller passed (its tz data, not ours) decides gaps and folds").
entities.details: Interop results can therefore differ from TemporalContext.resolve when the host's tz data and the rule bundle disagree.

entities.title: Standard library only
entities.summary: The package has no dependencies, and validates JSON with its own interpreter of the schema's keywords.
entities.decision: pyproject.toml declares dependencies = []. validate.py interprets the keywords the schema uses ($ref, type, const, enum, minLength, pattern, minItems, items, properties, required, additionalProperties, anyOf, oneOf, not) instead of using a JSON Schema package.
entities.details: The README and the code state the choice but not why it was made. A keyword the schema starts to use and the interpreter doesn't know is ignored by it.
